div.head: Another of the same kind; and it was composed with reference to Trimarius the dancer (ὀρχηστής) when the men who were making an entry (εἰσέλασμα) met him and compelled him to go another way.
270 — ii — VI. — I have been grieved in my meditation and have been confounded.

div.ab:
When I see that the lasciviousness of profligacy has
increased, and moreover consider also the great [burden of sins that is mine, and fear lest I perish by being swept away perforce by the rush of the stream of the evil deeds of this world, I groan and in distress utter the words of Jeremiah the prophet and say, Who will give me a remote habitation in the wilderness? and when left alone therein I will weep bitterly; and so, bathing the eyes of my mind with tears, I will look to thee [and say, O! Christ, with the divine prophet, Thou art my portion, Lord, I have said that I will keep thy law. I have looked for thy face (or I have entreated thy countenance) with my whole heart; have mercy upon me according to thy word and thy great mercy.

noteGrp.note: p. 305, n. 4 Ps. lv, 2 LXX. 18, 819 marg. This quotation is not in the Syriac, but stands in the Greek......
p. 306, n. 1 Corr. multitude of sins to myself.

p. 306, n. 3 Jer. ix, 2, 3 LXX Who will give me in the wilderness a remote habitation? and I will leave my people and will go from them, because they all commit adultery, and (are) an assembly of men who do iniquity. And they have stretched out their tongue as a bow, falsehood and not faith hath gained power over the land, because they have gone out from evil deeds to evil deeds, and me they have not known, saith the Lord.
p. 306, n. 6 Ps. cxviii, 57, 58 LXX Thou art my portion, Lord. I have said that I will keep thy law. I have entreated thy countenance with my whole heart, have mercy upon me according to thy word.
